title: Kernel auto-selection v2 — Kickoff notes (working doc)
linked_artifacts: Confluence:(draft) Kernel auto-selection v2 design doc
body:
Doc purpose
- Capture kickoff discussion + decisions + open questions for Kernel auto-selection v2.
- This is the “messy” working doc; design + ADR will live in Confluence once stabilized.

Meeting
- Date: 2026-01-09
- Organizer: Talia Benson
- Notes: Talia
- Working group cadence: 30 min 2x/week for Phase 0/1, then weekly.

Attendees
- Runtime Kernels: Hiro Tanaka, Grace Kim, Yuki Sato
- Scheduling/Runtime: Sofia Ivanova, Omar El-Sayed, Lena Fischer, Noah Patel
- Perf/Bench: Marcus Reed, Rina Kobayashi
- Correctness/Conformance: Anika Gupta
- Release/SRE: Connor O’Brien, Allison Grant

Why we’re doing this (problem statement)
- Kernel selection today is “mostly heuristic” and ends up brittle:
  - Different behavior across GPU SKUs (L4/A10/A100/H100) produces tail-latency variance.
  - New model families (or model metadata gaps) lead to unexpected regressions.
  - Debugging “why we got kernel X” is too hard without reading code + logs.
- Goal is to make selection explicit + data-driven while keeping safe rollback paths.

High-level goals (agreed)
1) Improve p95 latency and cost/token for mixed workloads by selecting kernels tuned for regime:
   - prefill vs decode
   - short vs long prompt/context
2) Reduce perf variance across GPU SKUs by making selection deterministic + explicit.
3) Make rollout safe:
   - selector v2 behind a feature flag
   - deterministic fallback to v1 selector
   - allow per-model-family (and possibly per-GPU) overrides
4) Observability improvements:
   - record selection decision context: selector version, kernel id, model family, seq bucket, GPU normalized sku
   - make it easy to correlate with latency/correctness
5) Regression prevention:
   - perf-canary thresholds in CI
   - benchmark-lab coverage across representative prompt distributions

Non-goals (confirmed)
- We are not writing new kernels from scratch in this project.
- No customer-facing API semantic changes.
- No major scheduler redesign; we’ll thread through minimal signals needed for selection.

Scope sketch (v2 selector)
- Inputs (what selector sees)
  - Model family taxonomy (arch + flags like GQA/MQA, sliding window, etc.)
  - Sequence-length “regime” signal:
    - prefill vs decode
    - effective context bucket (TBD exact bucketing)
  - GPU normalization:
    - sku (L4/A10/A100/H100 etc.)
    - capability class / SM / special cases (MIG/partitioning)
- Decision mechanism
  - Table-driven “registry”:
    - row keys: model family + regime bucket
    - column keys: gpu class/sku
    - cell: kernel id (+ any kernel config flags)
  - Fallback behavior
    - if unknown family / missing metadata / unrecognized gpu: fall back to safe kernel set (and/or v1)
    - deterministic tie-breaking (no random “best of”)

Key early decision (tentative; to be confirmed in ADR)
- Move from “pure heuristics” to “table-driven registry with rule fallback.”
  - Rationale: easier to reason about, easier to update without touching selection code, supports explicit review process.
  - Still keep a minimal heuristic layer for unknowns and safety.

Constraints / risks called out
- Correctness:
  - Wrong kernel can cause NaNs or rare shape mismatches. Need conformance tests that cover:
    - representative shapes per family
    - long-context edge cases
    - prefill/decode transitions
  - Safe fallback must prioritize correctness over speed.
- Telemetry cardinality:
  - Kernel choice labels can explode if we tag on raw model name or raw sequence length.
  - We must bucket lengths and use model_family vs model_id in metrics.
  - Sampling decisions must be clear (metrics vs traces vs logs).
- Determinism:
  - Selection must be stable for identical inputs to make perf comparisons sane.
- Compatibility:
  - Older GPUs + older model metadata must not break serving.
  - Unknown model family behavior must be “boring”: safe kernels + explicit metric to flag unknowns.

Initial open questions
(1) Model-family taxonomy
- What is the minimal set of families we support for v1 of the registry?
  - Proposal: Llama-family, Mistral-family, Qwen-family as first-class.
  - Add “Other/Unknown” with safe behavior.
- How do we map model metadata -> family?
  - Do we rely on model card metadata in our catalog, HF config, or runtime-probed properties?
  - Who owns the mapping rules long-term (runtime kernels vs model onboarding team)?

(2) Sequence-length bucketing
- What is the right bucket function?
  - Need buckets aligned to “kernel regime changes” not arbitrary percentiles.
  - Candidate buckets (example only):
    - prefill: 0–512, 513–2048, 2049–8192, 8193+
    - decode: 0–128, 129–512, 513–2048, 2049+
- What is “effective length” at selection time?
  - Prefill: prompt length is known.
  - Decode: context length grows; do we choose once at start, or re-evaluate?
  - Initial lean: choose on prefill, then decode uses a decode bucket based on current context at step boundaries (but we need to avoid churn).
- Scheduler integration:
  - Where do we get prefill vs decode signal reliably?
  - Need to be careful about batching mixing prefill+decode in same microbatch.

(3) GPU normalization / capability detection
- How to normalize SKU in a stable way across deployments?
  - A10 vs A10G naming, L4 variants, etc.
  - MIG: do we need “A100-40GB 1g.5gb” class distinctions or a capability class?
- Do we select by exact SKU or by “GPU class” (e.g., sm80, sm90)?
  - Likely both: registry uses normalized sku, with fallback to class.

(4) Registry update process
- Who can change the selection table and how is it reviewed?
  - Proposal: registry lives in runtime repo under versioned schema; PR requires perf + correctness signoff.
- Versioning semantics:
  - Do we tie registry version to runtime release, or allow config-delivered updates?
  - Tentative: ship with runtime release first; revisit “out-of-band registry updates” later.

(5) Rollout shape
- How do we gate enablement?
  - Hosted: feature flag by region + percent rollout.
  - Dedicated/Private: opt-in config then default-on later.
- Overrides:
  - Do we allow per-model-family override only, or per-model-id override too?
  - SRE preference: per-family by default; per-model-id for emergencies only due to complexity.

(6) What do we measure as success?
- Primary:
  - p95 latency improvement in mixed workload distributions (prefill-heavy + decode-heavy) vs selector v1.
  - reduced p95 variance across SKUs at same workload.
- Secondary:
  - fewer “mystery regressions” during new GPU/model additions.
  - ability to quickly identify selection decision in traces.

Owners / initial responsibilities
- Program mgmt / coordination: Talia Benson
- Overall architecture / interfaces: Noah Patel
- Selector v2 core logic: Grace Kim (lead), with Hiro Tanaka review
- GPU normalization: Yuki Sato (lead)
- Scheduler signal threading (prefill/decode + buckets): Lena Fischer (lead) + Omar El-Sayed
- Perf suite + benchmark plan:
  - Marcus Reed (perf suite owner)
  - Rina Kobayashi (benchmark harness)
- Conformance tests / correctness gates: Anika Gupta
- Rollout + release train: Connor O’Brien
- Observability standards / label limits: Allison Grant (coordinate with telemetry platform)

Short-term milestones (Phase 0 / first 2 weeks)
Week 1 (by 2026-01-16)
- [Grace] Draft selector v2 decision flow (pseudo-code + inputs) and share for review.
- [Noah] Define selection context struct (model family + seq bucket + gpu sku + selector version).
- [Yuki] Draft GPU normalization mapping table + detection approach; identify MIG edge cases.
- [Lena/Omar] Identify where in scheduler we can reliably tag prefill vs decode; propose minimal plumbing.
- [Marcus/Rina] Propose benchmark matrix (models x GPU x prompt distributions) and rough runtime.
- [Anika] Propose conformance coverage set (shapes, families, buckets) and how to run in CI.
- [Allison] Draft telemetry fields + initial cardinality constraints (what can be a label vs log-only).

Week 2 (by 2026-01-23)
- Convert kickoff outcomes into:
  - Confluence design doc skeleton
  - ADR draft for table-driven registry decision
- [Grace] Implement “registry read + lookup” stub behind feature flag, returning same as v1 for now.
- [Lena/Omar] Add seq bucket signal stub (even if coarse) to selection context.
- [Marcus] Add one end-to-end benchmark run comparing v1 vs “v2==v1” to validate measurement pipeline.

Decisions captured (tentative; confirm after ADR)
- Selector v2 will be table-driven for known model families, with safe fallback when unknown.
- We will require explicit telemetry for selection decisions (but will bucket and/or sample to avoid cardinality blowups).
- Conformance tests are mandatory before broad rollout (cannot rely on “perf only”).

Action items (tracked in Linear)
- ENG-3921: Umbrella project ticket (Talia to keep up to date)
- ENG-3922: Define model-family taxonomy and mapping rules (Noah + Grace)
- ENG-3923: Implement selector v2 core logic (Grace)
- ENG-3924: Seq-length bucketing signal + scheduler wiring (Lena + Omar)
- ENG-3925: GPU capability detection + normalization (Yuki)
- ENG-3926: Kernel registry schema + versioning (Hiro + Grace)
- ENG-3927: Telemetry for selection decisions (Allison coordinating; implementation owner TBD)
- ENG-3928: Conformance tests for selected kernels (Anika)
- ENG-3929: Benchmark-lab updates + report artifact (Rina)
- ENG-3930: Perf-canary gate integration (Marcus + Sahana Iyer)
- ENG-3931: Feature flag + overrides + kill switch (Connor + Benji Okafor)
- ENG-3932: Debug endpoint/CLI “explain selection” (Omar)

Notes / “parking lot”
- We should explicitly handle “unknown model family” with a metric counter and a runbook entry. We’ve been burned by “silently default to something fast.”
- Consider whether selection decision should be cached per (model_family, bucket, gpu) for hot paths.
- Keep an eye on “batch composition”: if a microbatch has mixed seq lengths, which bucket wins? Probably bucket by max effective length, but confirm.

Next meeting agenda (proposed)
- Review proposed model-family taxonomy + mapping inputs.
- Decide initial seq buckets (pick something we can ship; refine later).
- Decide initial GPU sku list we support in registry (L4, A10, A100, H100 as MVP).
- Telemetry: confirm labels vs log fields; agree on trace annotation format.
